texts.preamble: Britannia Industries Limited vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 29 February, 2024 Author: Abhay S. Oka
texts.facts: By the impugned order, four petitions filed by the appellant for quashing the prosecution for the offence punishable under Section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "the PFA Act") were dismissed. The allegation in the complaints was of misbranding, in the sense, that there was a violation of Rule 32(e) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short "the PFA Rules"). Rule 32(e) and 32(f) read thus: "Rule 32(e) A distinctive batch number or lot number or code number, either in numericals or alphabets or in combination, the numericals or alphabets or their combination, representing the batch number or lot number or code number being preceded by the words "Batch No." or Batch or 17:27:25 IST "Lot No." or "Lot" or any distinguishing prefix: Provided that in case of canned food, the batch number may be given at the bottom, or on the lid of the container, but the words "Batch No." given at the bottom or on the lid, shall appear on the body of the container. (f) the month and year in which the commodity is manufactured or prepacked; Provided also that in case of carbonated water containers and the packages of biscuits, confectionery and sweets, containing more than 60g. but not more than 120 g. and food packages weighing not Britannia Industries Limited vs The State Of Uttar Pradesh on 29 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8501887/ 1 more than 60 g. particulars under clauses (d) and (e) need not be specified;"
texts.arguments: The first submission of the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant is that Rule 32(e) in its earlier form was struck down by this Court in the case of Dwarka Nath & Anr. v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi1. His first submission is that the issue of validity of the amended rule on the basis of which the appellant was sought to be prosecuted was urged before the High Court. He submits that the law laid down by this Court in the case of Dwarka Nath1 will squarely apply to the Rule 32(e) in its new form. In the alternative, his submission is that there was a policy of the Government of Delhi that in case of first violation of the Rule 32(e), before filing the complaint, a notice is required to be served to the offender giving him an opportunity to rectify. He submitted that on the basis of the said 1. (1971) 2 SCC 314 policy, a large numbers of complaints have been [LEAKAGE_MASK] by the Delhi High Court.
